text: The following question stood in the name of  Dr Lim Wee Kiak –  11 To ask the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance since the introduction of the Pioneer Generation Package and the Merdeka Generation Package (a) how much of the budget set aside has been spent under each package respectively; (b) how many citizens have benefited from these packages and, of which, how many recipients are still alive; and (c) how has the rise in inflation impacted the budget for these packages.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (a) how many seniors have benefited from the Pioneer Generation Package and Merdeka Generation Package respectively; (b) how much money has been disbursed so far under each of the packages; (c) whether the funds set aside for both packages are adequate to meet future disbursements; and (d) whether projected surpluses, if any, can be used to enhance the benefits of both packages.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We established the PG Fund and MG Fund to set aside monies upfront for these packages.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This ensured the Government honours our commitment to PG and MG seniors, regardless of future economic or fiscal circumstances.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We sized the funds based on the projected lifetime cost, the benefits in the PG and MG packages, after accounting for inflation and interest accrued.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The Government will continue to review holistically our schemes and subsidy framework, and update the key parameters where needed, to ensure the affordability of healthcare for Singaporeans, including our PG and MG seniors.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: MOF and MOH review the sufficiency of the PG Fund and MG Fund every year.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is good to hear that there are 340,000 and 380,000 seniors benefiting from the PG and MG Fund.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The Senior Minister of State mentioned that there is a $6.1 billion and $5.72 billion balance in both the PG Fund and MG Fund.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Is it possible if some of these excess balances can be diverted or funnelled slightly to support or enhance the Silver Support package because there are some segments of the silver generation or seniors in Singapore that may benefit further from the Silver Support package being enhanced going forward?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat's question about Silver Support, I think this is a different objective from the PG and MG packages which are geared more towards providing for the healthcare and peace of mind of our PG and MG seniors.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And the conditions, as Members are aware, we will look at the housing type, the per capita household income and also the CPF balances at age 55.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, all these are designed to provide some additional help for seniors who, when they were younger, did not earn enough, did not accumulate enough CPF balances and when they grow old, when they retire, we give them some additional help through Silver Support.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, the objective is different from PG and MG, but we will look at both very carefully.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: For MG and PG, as I mentioned in my main reply, if it is necessary to top up these funds, the PG Fund and the MG Fund, we will do so to honour our commitments to our PG and MG seniors.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: For Silver Support, we have been regularly reviewing the amount and also the criteria to see how we can help our seniors who need this assistance when they retire.
